posts.name: Liftora AI
posts.cooked:
I’m building Liftora AI — an AI implementation business focused on helping businesses adopt AI, automate processes, and build practical AI solutions that actually save time and money.

I’m looking for a technical AI partnerto build this with me.

What I’ll handle:

  • Finding and onboarding clients
  • Sales & business development
  • Understanding client needs
  • Managing client relationships
  • Strategy, operations & the business side
  • Growing the company

What I’m looking for you to handle:

  • AI/automation architecture
  • Building and implementing AI solutions for clients
  • Integrations, agents, workflows & automations
  • Technical problem-solving
  • Choosing the right AI tools and technologies
  • Helping turn client requirements into working solutions

You don’t need to be a “10x software engineer.” I’m looking for someone who understands AI deeply, is hands-on, can build, experiment and figure things out, and is excited about turning AI into real business solutions.

This would be a partnership, not a traditional employee position. I’m looking for someone who wants to take ownership, build something from the ground up, and potentially grow this into a serious company.

You should ideally be:

  • Strong with AI tools, agents & automation
  • Technical and hands-on
  • A problem solver
  • Entrepreneurial and proactive
  • Good with communication
  • Excited about the opportunity AI is creating for businesses

I’ll focus on bringing the opportunities and running the business side. You’ll own the technical side.

If this sounds like something you’d be interested in, DM me with a little about yourself, your technical/AI experience, and a few examples of things you’ve built.

Liftora AI: liftoraai.com

posts.name: Reidgardas Zilinskas
posts.cooked:
Hi,

Your post is very close to the type of partnership I’m looking for.

I’m an independent automation builder based in Lithuania, focused on n8n, AI-assisted workflows, APIs/webhooks, CRM automation and business-process integrations.

I currently have 20+ practical workflows, including AI email triage, CRM lead intake and qualification, support/SLA automation, AI chatbot/knowledge-base workflows, order processing and a larger B2B prospect research/outreach system involving HTTP requests, JavaScript logic, data extraction, validation and AI-assisted processing.

I like the split you described: you focus on client acquisition, sales and client relationships, while I focus on technical implementation and delivery.

Before making a long-term co-founder commitment, I’d prefer to start with one real client/project and see how we work together.

How are you planning to structure project revenue/payment between the business and the technical partner, and do you currently have any active client opportunities?

I strongly prefer async written communication by email/chat.

If useful, I can send screenshots of several workflows I’ve built.

Best,

posts.name: David Buchan
posts.cooked:
A partnership conversation deserves a real foundation, so here’s the immediately useful version: once your client pipeline starts delivering, your ceiling is build capacity — how many clients you can sell before delivery chokes. I solve that side.

I take white-label bench work: fixed prices per scope, you keep the client relationship and the margin, I do the building — n8n/Make workflows, AI agents, integrations, voice-AI setups. Every delivery includes a video walkthrough plus written handoff notes, so it’s genuinely yours to support and looks like your team to the client.

Low-risk start: pick one small client task (or a slice of one) and I’ll quote it fixed. If we work well together, the co-founder conversation has real data behind it — which beats deciding on vibes either way.

posts.name: Djaouad Frih
posts.cooked:
Hi — I read your split: you take sales and client relationships, I take the technical build. That is exactly the shape I want, because I do not want to be the person selling.

What I’d bring to Liftora is the half that usually decides whether an AI implementation business is profitable or not: the part after the demo.

Most implementation work fails quietly. A client gets an agent, it works for two weeks, then latency drifts, token costs climb, a tool call starts returning garbage, and nobody notices until the client complains. Then you are debugging instead of selling. That is the problem I have already solved.

Every system I run has per-step LLM tracing on Langfuse — every tool call, every latency figure, every token cost, per request. When something degrades, you see it before the client does. For an implementation business that is the difference between a service and a liability.

Live, right now, if you want to see rather than read:

  • chat.djaouad.is-a.dev — multilingual booking agent
  • customer.djaouad.is-a.dev — support over WhatsApp
  • docs.djaouad.is-a.dev — document AI workspace

On your side I would also want to keep one thing honest: I’d rather be a partner than a subcontractor you have to manage. I don’t want you reselling my availability, and I don’t want to be the invisible developer behind your brand. The clients should know who built their system.

Two questions before we go further:

  1. Where are you based, and what hours overlap are you actually working in? I’m in Algeria — if you need US or EU daytime coverage I am going to tell you now rather than three weeks in.

  2. What kind of client do you want to start with? The first one decides almost everything about how the offer is shaped.

Best,
Djaouad Frih
Full-Stack + AI Engineer
djaouad.is-a.dev

posts.name: Oldrich Works
posts.cooked:
Hi, here is a slightly different shape than one co-founder, in case it fits: we are a small studio and could be Liftora’s delivery partner. You keep the clients, the sales and the relationship. We build under your name (white-label), at a fixed price per project that you mark up, or a revenue share if you prefer.

What we would take on

  • n8n / Make workflows, AI agents (support, lead qualification, document processing), API and CRM integrations
  • small web apps and dashboards when a client outgrows a workflow
  • written handover docs for every build, and we fix any bug of ours for free

What we can show: our agents run customer support for our own e-shop on five channels (median first reply 36 seconds), plus its ads, shop and analytics. We keep the full history of every project, so your clients never have to explain things twice.

Good to know: a first deal usually stalls on scoping, not on building. Send us your call notes and we turn them into a written scope and a fixed quote within a day, so you can price it while the client is still warm.

A simple way to test it: one real client request, we scope and quote it, you decide.

Is there already one client request on your table? Paste the brief here or in a message and we start with that one.

We work in writing (no phone or WhatsApp). Reply here or message @oldrichworks.

P.S. Oldrich, the owner, supervises the work and stands behind every result. We use various tools and AI agents to work fast and efficiently.
